title: Emergency contracts still being paid years later
question: Which contracts that began three or more years before July 2025 were still drawing payments under an emergency purchasing rule in fiscal 2026 and 2027?
finding: 25 contracts that started before July 2022 were still being paid under an emergency purchasing rule in fiscal 2026 or 2027, drawing $34.8 million in those two years. 25 of the 25 are Homelessness Services grants. 23 contracts awarded under emergency rules since July 2018 have a term of five years or more ($220.6 million agreed); the latest is scheduled to end on 2030-06-30.
how: Payments under a rule containing the word "emergency" were added up by contract number and by the fiscal year in which each was issued, read from its voucher number. A contract is listed when the Supplier Contracts table gives it a start date before 1 July 2022 and it drew $50,000 or more under that rule in fiscal 2026 and 2027 together. Age is counted from the start date to 9 November 2026, the date of the payment file.
limits: The Board extended its waiver of bidding for homelessness contracts to May 2029, according to the Homelessness Department’s own sole-source report, so a grant first made as an emergency may now rest on that waiver while the payment file still shows the old wording. The record does not name the emergency. A long-running shelter or housing program cannot be re-bid without moving the people in it, which is a real cost of competition. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days. Payments that belong to fiscal 2018 or earlier are in none of the figures here.
